AI Grievance Management System

spark

Gemini

BUILD A COMPLETE AI-POWERED PUBLIC GRIEVANCE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM

Build a professional, modern, fully functional AI-Powered Public Grievance Management System for a hackathon project.

The system should be inspired by the concept and workflow of the Government of India's CPGRAMS (Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System), but this must be an original prototype and must NOT pretend to be the official CPGRAMS website.

The project should demonstrate how AI can improve public grievance registration, department classification, prioritization, tracking, routing, and analytics.

1. PROJECT NAME

AI Grievance Management System

Subtitle:

AI-Powered Smart Public Grievance Registration, Routing & Monitoring Platform

Add a small note:

"Prototype inspired by public grievance systems such as CPGRAMS."

Do not use government logos or claim that this application is an official government portal.

2. MAIN PROBLEM

Citizens face difficulties when submitting complaints because:

  • They may not know which department is responsible.

  • Complaints can be sent to the wrong department.

  • Manual complaint classification takes time.

  • Important/high-priority complaints can be difficult to identify.

  • Citizens may not know the current status of their complaint.

  • Different departments receive large numbers of complaints.

  • Complaint data is difficult to analyze manually.

  • Duplicate or similar complaints may exist.

  • Officers may have difficulty identifying urgent cases.

  • Citizens may have to repeatedly contact departments for updates.

The proposed system solves these problems using AI.

3. CORE IDEA

A citizen submits a complaint using:

  • Text

  • Optional image

  • Optional supporting document

  • Category

  • Location

  • Preferred language

The AI analyzes the complaint and automatically:

  1. Understands the complaint.

  2. Detects the category.

  3. Identifies the most appropriate department.

  4. Assigns priority.

  5. Detects possible duplicate/similar complaints.

  6. Generates a complaint summary.

  7. Creates a complaint/ticket ID.

  8. Routes it to the appropriate department.

  9. Allows the citizen to track only their own complaint.

  10. Provides department officers with relevant department-specific complaints.

  11. Provides administrators with authorized aggregate analytics.

4. IMPORTANT PRIVACY RULE

THIS IS EXTREMELY IMPORTANT.

Do NOT create a public page where a citizen can view all complaints submitted by everyone.

A normal citizen/user must ONLY be able to access:

  • Their own complaints

  • Their own complaint IDs

  • Their own complaint status

  • Their own submitted information

  • Their own uploaded files

  • Updates related to their own complaints

  • Their own complaint history

Never expose:

  • Other citizens' names

  • Other citizens' phone numbers

  • Other citizens' addresses

  • Other citizens' complaint descriptions

  • Other citizens' documents

  • Other citizens' complaint IDs

  • Other citizens' personal information

The "Track Complaint" page must require a complaint ID and appropriate verification/login.

Do not create a "View All Complaints" page for citizens.

5. USER ROLES

Create role-based access.

ROLE 1 — CITIZEN

Citizen can:

  • Register/login

  • Submit complaint

  • Upload image/document

  • Track own complaint

  • View own complaint history

  • Receive status updates

  • View AI-generated department suggestion

  • View AI-generated priority

  • Contact support

  • Logout

Citizen CANNOT:

  • View other citizens' complaints

  • View department-wide complaint databases

  • View admin analytics

  • Modify another person's complaint

  • Access officer dashboards

ROLE 2 — DEPARTMENT OFFICER

Department officers can only access complaints assigned to their department.

Example:

A Municipal Officer should see relevant municipal complaints.

A Water Department Officer should see water-related complaints.

A Transport Officer should see transport-related complaints.

An Electricity Officer should see electricity-related complaints.

Officers can:

  • View assigned complaints

  • View complaint details

  • Update status

  • Add official remarks

  • Assign complaint to an appropriate internal team

  • Mark complaint as resolved

  • Request additional information

  • See priority

  • See AI-generated summary

  • See similar/duplicate complaint suggestions

Officers must NOT see unrelated departments' private complaint information.

ROLE 3 — ADMIN

Admin has a broader authorized view.

Admin can see:

  • Overall complaint statistics

  • Department-wise complaint counts

  • Priority distribution

  • Resolution rates

  • Average resolution time

  • Pending complaints

  • Resolved complaints

  • Complaint trends

  • AI classification accuracy/demo statistics

  • Department performance

Admin should see analytics and aggregated information rather than unnecessarily exposing citizens' personal information.

6. MULTIPLE GOVERNMENT DEPARTMENTS

Create realistic departments.

At minimum include:

  1. Municipal Administration

  2. Water Supply & Sanitation

  3. Roads & Transport

  4. Electricity

  5. Public Health

  6. Education

  7. Revenue & Land Services

  8. Police / Public Safety

  9. Housing

  10. Social Welfare

  11. Environment

  12. Rural Development

The system should allow more departments to be added later.

7. AI DEPARTMENT CLASSIFICATION

When a citizen submits a complaint, AI should analyze the complaint and suggest the most relevant department.

Example:

Citizen complaint:

"There has been a large pothole near our college entrance for several weeks."

AI result:

Category: Road Damage

Suggested Department: Roads & Transport

Priority: High

Reason:

"Road damage may create a safety risk for commuters."

Another example:

"Our street has had no water supply for three days."

AI result:

Category: Water Supply

Suggested Department: Water Supply & Sanitation

Priority: High

Another example:

"The streetlights in our area have not been working."

AI result:

Category: Street Lighting

Suggested Department: Municipal Administration

Priority: Medium

The AI should not blindly assign a department.

Show:

AI Suggested Department

and allow an authorized officer/admin to correct the classification when necessary.

8. AI PRIORITY CLASSIFICATION

AI should classify complaints into:

  • Critical

  • High

  • Medium

  • Low

Priority should be based on factors such as:

  • Public safety risk

  • Number of people potentially affected

  • Urgency

  • Essential service disruption

  • Severity

  • Location sensitivity

  • Potential public health impact

Example:

"Open manhole near a school"

→ Critical/High

"Water supply stopped for multiple days"

→ High

"Streetlight not working"

→ Medium

"Request for general information"

→ Low

Do not claim that the AI decision is legally binding.

Display:

AI Priority Suggestion

9. AI COMPLAINT SUMMARY

After submission, automatically generate a concise summary.

Example:

Original:

"There is a huge pothole near our college road and many students are facing problems while travelling. It has been there for almost one month."

AI Summary:

"Large pothole near a college road causing travel difficulties for students for approximately one month."

Show the summary to the officer.

Complaint B:
"Road damaged near Main Road."

"Potentially similar complaint detected."

Do NOT automatically merge complaints without authorization.

Allow authorized officers/admins to review and decide.

build Built

I have built the AI Grievance Management System, a smart public grievance registration, routing, and monitoring platform inspired by India's CPGRAMS framework.

Key Highlights & Architecture

  • AI-Powered Grievance Intake & Classification:

    • Natural Language Parsing: Citizens can submit grievances in plain English, Telugu, or Hindi without needing prior knowledge of administrative jurisdictions.

    • Automated Department Identification: Gemini AI maps grievances across 12 government departments (Roads & Transport, Water Supply & Sanitation, Electricity & Power, Municipal Administration, Public Health, Education, Revenue & Land, Police & Traffic, Women & Child Development, Environmental Protection, Public Distribution System, and Social Welfare).

    • Urgency & Safety Assessment: Automatically evaluates public safety risks and flags critical hazards (e.g. sparking wires, open manholes, health outbreaks) for accelerated 24-hour SLA remediation.

    • Executive Summarization & Duplicate Detection: Condenses citizen narratives into concise briefings for field engineers and identifies similar issues reported nearby.

    • Zero-Failure Fallback Engine: If the AI API reaches rate limits, a deterministic heuristic engine ensures continuous, uninterrupted classification and assistance.

  • Strict Privacy by Design Architecture:

    • Citizen Data Isolation: Public listings of all complaints are strictly disallowed. Citizens can only access, track, and review their own submitted grievances.

    • Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Distinct permissions for Citizens (own grievances), Department Officers (department-specific queues, status updates, field crew dispatch, and reassignment), and Administrators (aggregate metrics, spatial heatmaps, SLA tracking, and data export).

    • AI Assistant Guardrails: The conversational AI Assistant helps draft complaints, explains tracking stages, and actively blocks unauthorized queries seeking access to other citizens' personal data.

  • Complete Redressal Workflow & Portals:

    • 7-Stage Lifecycle Timeline: Interactive visual tracking (Submitted → AI Classified → Assigned → Under Review → In Progress → Resolved → Closed / Need Information / Reopened).

    • Digital Acknowledgment Slip: Downloadable, printable receipts with unique IDs (e.g. GRV-2026-10482), QR seals, and target SLA dates.

    • Citizen Redressal Actions: 1-to-5 star satisfaction rating on resolution and formal grievance reopening with justification notes.

    • Officer Remediation Console: Status updates with mandatory official remarks, field team assignments, and inter-departmental transfer logs.

    • Admin Command Center: Visual analytics by department, priority, status, spatial districts, and automated AI trend insights.

    • Interactive Demo Switcher: 1-click switching between Citizen, Officer, and Admin accounts to evaluate role-based isolation during demonstrations.

I have applied the Sleek Interface design theme across the entire application:

  • Typography & Canvas Structure: Applied Space Grotesk for headings and display labels, paired with Plus Jakarta Sans for crisp, legible body text and JetBrains Mono for IDs and timestamps on a clean, high-contrast neutral slate background.

  • Card & Component Hierarchy: Standardized all metric cards, forms, and tables with rounded corners (rounded-2xl), subtle hairline borders (border-slate-200/90 in light mode, border-slate-800 in dark sections), and soft drop shadows.

  • Sleek Dark Accents: Enhanced telemetry insights and banner sections with deep slate-950 backgrounds, subtle glowing badge accents, and high-contrast typography.

  • Control & Input Refinements: Updated search bars, filters, buttons, and modal dialogs with smooth hover transitions, clear active states, and standardized padding.
